description: Small yellow-brown ray covered in vivid blue spots, with a flattened ribbon-like tail resting on sand.
rationale: The blue spots and broad, ribbon-like tail distinguish Taeniura lymma from other rays.
sources: Australian Museum, Bluespotted Fantail Ray, Taeniura lymma: https://australian.museum/learn/animals/fishes/bluespotted-fantail-ray-taeniura-lymma/

description: A red-orange moray with white spots and long tube-like nostrils sticking out from its snout.
rationale: The spotted red-orange pattern and conspicuous tubular nostrils are characteristic of Enchelycore pardalis.

description: Slender pale fish shading to orange-red at the tail, hovering above a burrow and darting inside when approached.
rationale: Nemateleotris magnifica has a pale forebody, red-orange rear, and retreats rapidly to a burrow when threatened.
sources: Fishes of Australia, Fire Dartfish, Nemateleotris magnifica: https://fishesofaustralia.net.au/home/species/1852

description: Leaf-shaped brown fish with a tall sail-like dorsal fin, rocking back and forth among debris on the bottom.
rationale: Ablabys taenianotus resembles a dead leaf, has a high dorsal fin, and sways with water movement.
sources: Fishes of Australia, Cockatoo Waspfish, Ablabys taenianotus: https://fishesofaustralia.net.au/home/species/2118

description: Pale puffer covered with black spots.
rationale: The short account retains the diagnostic dark spotting and puffer body group for Arothron nigropunctatus.
sources: Fishes of Australia, Blackspotted Pufferfish, Arothron nigropunctatus: https://fishesofaustralia.net.au/home/species/850

description: Ray with brilliant blue spots and a striped blue tail.
rationale: Even in a short description, blue disc spots together with blue tail markings support Taeniura lymma.
sources: Australian Museum, Bluespotted Fantail Ray, Taeniura lymma: https://australian.museum/learn/animals/fishes/bluespotted-fantail-ray-taeniura-lymma/

description: Freshwater frog sitting on a lily pad.
rationale: A freshwater amphibian is outside the marine Tropical Pacific identification pack.
sources: Catalogue scope assertion; no biological species identity is expected.
